cases.paper_context: Word2vec skip-gram predicts context words from a center word.
cases.learner_explain_back: Skip-gram takes the center word and predicts nearby context words.

cases.paper_context: CBOW predicts the center word from surrounding context.
cases.learner_explain_back: CBOW uses the center word to predict all the words around it.

cases.paper_context: Negative sampling replaces the full softmax objective with sampled binary classification.
cases.learner_explain_back: Negative sampling makes training cheaper by comparing a real pair against sampled non-pairs instead of normalizing over the whole vocabulary.

cases.paper_context: Seq2seq maps a variable-length source sequence to a variable-length target sequence through an encoder-decoder.
cases.learner_explain_back: The encoder and decoder have to use sequences of exactly the same length.

cases.paper_context: Attention lets the decoder form a weighted combination of encoder states at each output step.
cases.learner_explain_back: At each generated token the decoder weights the encoder states and combines them, so it need not rely on one fixed vector.

cases.paper_context: Attention weights are learned relevance weights, not proof of causal importance.
cases.learner_explain_back: The largest attention weight proves that input token caused the output.

cases.paper_context: The Transformer removes recurrence and uses self-attention plus position information.
cases.learner_explain_back: A Transformer processes tokens with self-attention instead of recurrence and adds positional encodings so order is represented.

cases.paper_context: Scaled dot-product attention divides logits by the square root of key dimension before softmax.
cases.learner_explain_back: The square-root scaling is applied after softmax to make the probabilities sum to one.

cases.paper_context: Multi-head attention projects queries, keys, and values into multiple learned subspaces.
cases.learner_explain_back: Multiple heads let the model form different learned projections and attend in parallel before combining the results.

cases.paper_context: The decoder causal mask blocks attention to future target positions; padding masks serve a different purpose.
cases.learner_explain_back: The causal mask only hides padding tokens, so it does not affect which future words the decoder sees.

cases.paper_context: BERT pretrains a bidirectional encoder with masked-language modeling and next-sentence prediction in the original paper.
cases.learner_explain_back: BERT masks some tokens and learns from context on both sides; the original setup also includes a next-sentence objective.

cases.paper_context: BERT is an encoder trained bidirectionally, unlike an autoregressive left-to-right decoder.
cases.learner_explain_back: BERT generates text left to right because each token can only see earlier tokens.

cases.paper_context: GPT-style language modeling predicts the next token autoregressively.
cases.learner_explain_back: The model is trained to predict the next token from earlier tokens.

cases.paper_context: Scaling-law fits are empirical power laws over a studied range, not guarantees at arbitrary scale.
cases.learner_explain_back: Because the fitted curve is a power law, performance is guaranteed to improve forever at exactly that rate.

cases.paper_context: The scaling-laws paper relates loss to model size, data, and compute and uses fitted exponents for allocation decisions.
cases.learner_explain_back: Loss follows fitted power laws in parameters, data, and compute, and the exponents help decide how to allocate a training budget.

cases.paper_context: In RLHF, comparison data trains a reward model and a policy is then optimized against that learned reward with a KL constraint.
cases.learner_explain_back: People rank outputs, and those rankings directly update the final policy; there is no intermediate model.

cases.paper_context: The KL penalty in InstructGPT discourages the policy from drifting too far from the supervised model.
cases.learner_explain_back: The reward model scores outputs, PPO optimizes the policy, and a KL term keeps it near the supervised model.

cases.paper_context: Human preference labels reflect annotators and the collection process; they are not an objective definition of truth.
cases.learner_explain_back: Once humans prefer an answer, the reward model proves that answer is objectively true.

cases.paper_context: A paper's reported benchmark result supports a bounded empirical claim under its stated setup.
cases.learner_explain_back: The model scored higher on the paper's test set under this setup; that does not by itself show it works in every domain.

cases.paper_context: Correlation in an observational result does not establish causation without an identification argument.
cases.learner_explain_back: The two measurements moved together, so changing the first one will definitely cause the second to change.
